clue.text: Twerk in deepest Slough?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: to twerk is to rock one's bottom
second meaning: the lowest point, the depths of a slough of despond

explanation.surface: A jibe that the dance craze is found deep in the unloved Berkshire town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a Berkshire town often mocked, but here it is a slough, a bog or state of despair, as in Bunyan's Slough of Despond.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the lowest possible level, while twerking literally involves shaking one's rear end.

clue.text: Risqué introduction to column in issue of The Sun

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, the word in telling us which sits within

parts.note: a ray is what the sun emits

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter of column

explanation.surface: A tabloid column in The Sun opens with something saucy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun looks like the newspaper, but its issue is a sunbeam.
explanation.definitionFit: Racy and risqué are synonyms, both describing slightly indecent humour or content.

clue.text: Dismiss bank employee

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to discharge from the armed forces in disgrace
second meaning: a teller who handles money at a counter

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests sacking a bank worker; the verb and the noun are the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to discharge an officer in disgrace; as a noun it is the person handling payments in a bank.

clue.text: Badger to acquire trendy novel

indicators.note: to acquire is to take something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: brock is an old name for a badger
right-on means fashionably progressive

explanation.surface: An instruction to pester someone into buying a fashionable book.
explanation.walkthrough: Badger looks like a verb meaning nag; it is the animal. The trendy word slots in after the first letter. BRIGHTON ROCK is Graham Greene's novel; the rock is also a seaside candy stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton Rock is a 1938 crime novel by Graham Greene set in the English seaside town.

clue.text: Corrupt MP wrote about a parasite

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the letters are wrapped around the little word that follows
something corrupt has been twisted out of its proper form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sleazy politician has written a piece about a bloodsucker.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapeworm is a flat worm that lives as a parasite in the intestines of its host.

clue.text: Oscar certainly not turning up for prayer

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: 'No, sir!' is an emphatic refusal

explanation.surface: An Oscar is definitely not going to appear, so one must pray for it.
explanation.definitionFit: An orison is an old literary word for a prayer, used by Shakespeare in Hamlet.

clue.text: An element of the unknown elected head of committee

parts.note: z is a standard algebraic unknown
a winning candidate is voted in

indicators.note: the head is the top, so only the first letter of the following word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of committee

explanation.surface: Part of the mystery around who has been elected to chair the committee.
explanation.walkthrough: An element reads as a part of something; it is a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is a metallic chemical element, atomic number 30.

clue.text: Current Conservative, Green and Liberal Democrat at zero?

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
eco- denotes green, environmental concerns
LD is the abbreviation for Liberal Democrat

explanation.surface: A political roll-call of today's parties, all apparently polling at nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The parties look like a political list but are just abbreviations; Conservative and Liberal Democrat are British parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius, so something at zero is freezing cold; the question mark flags the loose definition.

clue.text: Film stylish toy boy Bruno getting undressed

parts.note: chic means fashionably elegant
Ken is the boy doll, Barbie's boyfriend

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of its outer covering, so only the inner letters of the name remain

parts.note: the name with its outer letters removed

explanation.surface: A racy film about a stylish young lover named Bruno taking his clothes off.
explanation.walkthrough: Toy boy looks like a young lover; it is literally a toy, the Ken doll.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken Run is the 2000 Aardman stop-motion animated film about hens escaping a farm.

clue.text: Charlie, Charlie & Ivor, Piet, Ivan oddly formed a group of stars

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a charlie is British slang for a fool

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-numbered letters, the first, third, fifth and so on

parts.note: the odd letters of these three names

explanation.surface: A list of five chaps who together formed a starry ensemble.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Charlies do different jobs: one is the phonetic letter, the other the slang word for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassiopeia is a W-shaped constellation in the northern sky, named after a mythical queen.

clue.text: Food store I ran after retiring

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written
to run a firm is to lead it

explanation.surface: A retired person recalls the grocery shop they used to manage.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling prepared foods such as cold meats and cheeses.

clue.text: Deny a casino's organised special occasion

indicators.note: organised means arranged into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: Someone refuses a casino's planned special event.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascension Day is a Christian feast marking Christ's ascent to heaven, a special day in the church calendar.

clue.text: Mine host's principal point of substance

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

indicators.note: principal means first, so only the opening letter of the word before is taken

parts.note: the first letter of host

explanation.surface: The landlord's key argument, 'mine host' being an old phrase for a pub landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine host' is a set phrase for an innkeeper, but here mine is the pit.
explanation.definitionFit: The pith of an argument is its essential core, the point that carries the substance.

clue.text: Court enclosure for accused holding small time accomplice of Joe Cool?

indicators.note: holding means keeping something within, so the small pieces go inside

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them
the dock is where the defendant stands in court
S is the abbreviation for small
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A courtroom scene where the defendant's box holds a brief moment with a criminal's sidekick.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Cool is Snoopy's sunglasses-wearing alter ego in Peanuts, and Woodstock is his little yellow bird friend. The two small letters go just after the first letter of the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodstock is the bird who is Snoopy's constant companion in the Peanuts comic strip.

clue.text: Quick shot through the covers that sticks in the memory?

parts.note: in a flash means very quickly
a cover drive is a cricket stroke hit through the covers, a fielding area

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator recalls a brisk stroke through the covers that remains unforgettable.
explanation.walkthrough: The covers are a fielding area on the off side in cricket. The definition is a pun: the device is a memory stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A flash drive is a USB memory stick, a device that stores data in flash memory.

clue.text: Pig fat sandwiches left for sailors once

indicators.note: to sandwich is to enclose between two layers, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: lard is pig fat
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: Pork dripping is spread in sandwiches and left out for sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pig fat' reads as one phrase meaning lard, but the pig and the fat are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Larboard is the old nautical term for the port, left-hand side of a ship, replaced to avoid confusion with starboard.

clue.text: In Calais, the port is dull

parts.note: le is French for the, as spoken in Calais
Aden is a port city in Yemen

explanation.surface: A traveller's verdict that the French ferry port of Calais is boring.
explanation.walkthrough: The port seems to be Calais itself, but Calais only signals French; the port is another one.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaden means heavy and lifeless, so a dull, uninspiring thing can be called leaden.

clue.text: Alf turned up on deck eating a bit of jammy pancake

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the name is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a deck of cards is a pack

indicators.note: a bit is a small part, here just the first letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of jammy

explanation.surface: Alf appears on the ship's deck nibbling a jam-covered pancake.
explanation.walkthrough: Deck looks like a ship's deck; it is a deck of cards. In Britain a flapjack is usually an oat bar, but the name is also used for a pancake.
explanation.definitionFit: Flapjack is an old and North American word for a thick pancake cooked on a griddle.

clue.text: Big game here — listing starters, Sir Alex Ferguson announces Ronaldo, inevitably

indicators.note: starters are first things, so the first letter of each following word is listed

parts.words: Sir Alex Ferguson announces Ronaldo, inevitably
parts.note: the initial letters of these six words

explanation.surface: Football talk: the famous Manchester United manager unveils Ronaldo for a big match.
explanation.walkthrough: Big game looks like a football match, matching the Ferguson and Ronaldo scene, but it means large wild animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an expedition to see or hunt large wild animals, known as big game.

clue.text: Some suffer mental agitation

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the letters lie within a stretch of the following words

parts.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: Some people endure psychological distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferment can mean a state of unrest or excitement, as in a nation in ferment.

clue.text: Jobless youngster embraces vicar's kindness?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within, so the letters sit inside the phrase before

parts.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: A clergyman shows compassion to an unemployed young person.
explanation.walkthrough: A vicar blessing a person is his kindness, and the phrase is also what one says kindly after a sneeze.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a priestly benediction and a polite response, a gesture of goodwill from clergy.

clue.text: Famous artist: variable, niche, upwardly mobile, bespectacled

parts.note: y is a standard algebraic variable

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving upwards means the word is read from bottom to top
wearing glasses means surrounded by a pair of lenses, so the word goes inside them

parts.note: two round lenses look like a pair of letter Os
a nook is a small recess

explanation.surface: A profile of an artist: unpredictable, specialised, socially climbing and wearing glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: Spectacles give two Os, which wrap the upturned recess.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoko Ono is a Japanese conceptual artist and musician, widow of John Lennon, famous for her round glasses.

clue.text: Study old verse — the first from Ovid — afresh

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room for work
O is the abbreviation for old
V is the abbreviation for verse

indicators.note: the first means only the opening letter of the poet's name is taken

parts.note: the first letter of Ovid

explanation.surface: Advice to reread old Latin poetry, starting with Ovid, with fresh eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: Study looks like a verb but it is a room.
explanation.definitionFit: De novo is Latin for from the beginning, meaning starting again anew.

clue.text: Beginning to draw pie chart, freely available for next to nothing

indicators.note: freely means without restraint, so the letters are let loose into a new order
a beginning is the opening, so only the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter of draw
the letters of this phrase rearranged

explanation.surface: A tip to start drawing a pie chart for free.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirt cheap means extremely inexpensive, priced at almost nothing.

clue.text: Having taste of the barrel right after stomach upset?

indicators.note: the stomach is the middle of the body, so the middle letters of the word are upset and jumbled

parts.note: okay means all right

explanation.surface: A wine taster recovering from a bad stomach notes a woody flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: Stomach seems to be a real stomach upset, but it means the middle of the word, whose two central letters swap.
explanation.definitionFit: Wines matured in oak casks pick up a flavour described as oaky, a taste of the barrel.

clue.text: A short distance down

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a winning margin in horse racing
second meaning: to drink quickly, British slang for knocking back a drink

explanation.walkthrough: Down reads as a direction but is the verb to swallow a drink fast; to neck a pint is British slang for that.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse winning by a neck wins narrowly, and to neck a drink is to gulp it down.

clue.text: Setter's entertaining extremely tactile couple

indicators.note: to entertain is to receive as a guest, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: the setter is I, so the setter's is I am, contracted

indicators.note: extremely refers to the extremes, so only the outer letters of the following word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of tactile

explanation.surface: The setter describes enjoying the company of a very touchy-feely couple.
explanation.walkthrough: Setter's here means setter is, the contraction of I am.
explanation.definitionFit: Item is informal for a couple in a romantic relationship, as in 'they're an item'.

clue.text: A ringer for Reggie Kray?

parts.note: surface reading: a lookalike or double of the notorious East End gangster
setter's reading: a ringer is a telephone, named the way a Cockney such as Kray would say it

explanation.walkthrough: Reggie Kray was an East London gangster, so he speaks Cockney rhyming slang, where a phrase rhyming with a word replaces it; the answer rhymes with phone.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang this phrase stands for phone, the device that rings.

clue.text: Has DeSantis regularly lost?

indicators.note: losing letters at regular intervals means every other letter is dropped and the rest kept

parts.note: the even-numbered letters of the name

explanation.surface: A question about whether the Florida governor Ron DeSantis has been beaten again.
explanation.walkthrough: Has looks like an auxiliary verb but means consumes, as in has lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a meal is to eat it, so has can stand for eats.

clue.text: Labour perform vital task, stealing focus from Sunak

indicators.note: stealing means taking something in, so a piece is slipped inside the rest

parts.note: to perform an action is to do it

indicators.note: a focus is the centre, so only the middle letter of the name is taken

parts.note: the central letter of Sunak
key means crucial
a task is a piece of work

explanation.surface: Political commentary: the Labour Party does important work while drawing attention away from Rishi Sunak.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour looks like the British political party, matching Sunak, the former Conservative prime minister; it means toil.
explanation.definitionFit: Donkey work is the hard, tedious part of a job, the drudgery or toil.
